subject: glucose
group: suspected type 1 diabetes in a child (secondary enuresis)
correct: In a child with polyuria/polydipsia/weight loss, a random glucose ≥11.1 mmol/L (not >11.1) supports diabetes, and a capillary reading is not by itself a formal diagnosis. NICE NG18 says refer immediately (same day) to the paediatric diabetes team and do not wait for confirmatory tests.
source: https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng18 (rec 1.1.1–1.1.2: suspected T1D → same-day referral to multidisciplinary paediatric diabetes team); WHO diagnostic threshold random plasma glucose ≥11.1 mmol/L with symptoms

fixes.new: A random glucose of 11.1 mmol/L or more with these symptoms strongly suggests diabetes; do not wait for confirmatory tests: refer the same day to the paediatric diabetes team (NICE NG18).

note: The threshold sign is wrong (> instead of ≥). Calling a capillary reading a 'diagnosis' could also encourage the GP to confirm it in primary care before referring, which NG18 advises against. The adjacent cell ('>11.1 → same-day paediatric diabetes team') is acceptable in context.

subject: glucose
correct: Endocrine Society (Cryer 2009) criteria: plasma glucose <3.0 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) with insulin ≥3 µU/mL (≥18 pmol/L), C-peptide ≥0.6 ng/mL (≥0.2 nmol/L) and proinsulin ≥5 pmol/L. <2.2 mmol/L (40 mg/dL) is an older criterion.
source: https://academic.oup.com/jcem/article/94/3/709/2596186 (Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline: Evaluation and management of adult hypoglycemic disorders, 2009)
note: The insulin, C-peptide and proinsulin cut-offs in the same sentence already match the Endocrine Society criteria. Only the glucose threshold is out of date. This is a secondary-care teaching point, so it is low priority.

subject: glucose
group: type 2 diabetes safety-net: same-day contact threshold
correct: No national figure. Typical sick-day / safety-net advice is to contact the team if glucose stays high (commonly >15 mmol/L) despite usual treatment or extra measures, or at once with ketones, vomiting or dehydration.
source: https://trend-uk.org/ (TREND-UK 'What to do when you are ill' type 2 leaflet); https://www.diabetes.org.uk/guide-to-diabetes/life-with-diabetes/illness
note: OWNER: tools/management/type-2-diabetes.html, type-2-diabetes-print.html and summaries/type-2-diabetes.html (and assets/search/idx-protocol.json) say 'Same-day if… glucose persistently >20 for 48 hours'. Waiting 48 h at >20 mmol/L may delay recognition of HHS or DKA (on an SGLT2i), especially in older or unwell patients. Consider a lower or shorter trigger in line with the local sick-day leaflet, e.g. 'glucose persistently above 15 mmol/L (or your agreed level) for 24 hours, or any high reading with vomiting, dehydration, drowsiness or ketones'. This is not a national threshold, so it is the owner's choice.
